newsitem.title: USA: United American gets Florida approval.
newsitem.headline: United American gets Florida approval.

text.p: United American Healthcare Corp said Wednesday it was approved by the state of Florida to participate in the state's mandatory Medicaid initiative.

"We see things turning around in Florida," Julius Combs, chairman, said in a statement. "Since January 1997, our membership in UltraMedix Health Care Systems, the HMO (health maintenance organization) we manage in Florida, has grown from 9,900 to about 14,200, in both Medicaid and commercial markets, and we expect this growth to continue."
United American manages four HMOs under long-term contracts and provides management and advisory services to companies who self-fund their health care benefit plans.
Separately, United American said it repurchased 25,000 of its outstanding shares.

"We are very confident in the fundamentals of our business and continue to see them improving," Combs said. "We believe that our stock is extremely undervalued given our growth rate of both our revenues and membership. At less than 0.25 times sales, we believe our stock is a bargain and we plan to pursue additional purchases."
United American shares closed Tuesday at 4-5/8.
